# Sell to your first 100 customers: the minimalist entrepreneur playbook

Selected by Skill Harbor — short listing (the repo states no license, so no content is reproduced): @slavingia's first-customers skill — a business-advisor agent channeling the philosophy of "The Minimalist Entrepreneur" by Sahil Lavingia (Gumroad founder): skip the launch, focus on selling; the core principle that "viral success" is a myth and every overnight success is built on months of hard work. The concentric circles of sales (sell outward from friends-and-family to community to cold strangers), sales reframed as education not persuasion, pricing guidance (charge something — the zero-price effect; cost-based vs value-based; start low and raise), key metrics (manual sales = 99% of early growth; product-market fit = repeat customers), the rule to not launch until 100 paying customers (launch as a celebration, not an acquisition strategy), and a concrete output (lists of 10 friends/family and 10 community members to pitch this week, a cold-outreach template, an initial pricing strategy, a weekly sales goal). Honest caveats: business coaching, not software — the example cold email in the skill is from 2014-era Gumroad outreach, adapt it to your product; license not stated by the source repo — short listing with a link only, nothing copied. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
